headline: 6 Oct tape. Book A$4.43m. Options on the mid.
lede: The August notes are off this read. This is the 6 Oct US close. Book A$4.43m after every option line was remarked to the bid/ask mid (about A$46k of catch-up versus the prior marks, and that catch-up is not the session change). Marvell's Investor Day and a record Nvidia close are the story. Session stock move about A$17.8k, led by ALAB, MRVL, AVGO and AMD. Memory gave some back. EBTC is still the prior ASX mark. ATOM.AX stays sold.

items.title: Marvell Investor Day: FY28 about $20b, FY31 $70–90b
items.what: Tuesday 6 Oct, New York. Matt Murphy raised the FY28 revenue target to about $20 billion, from about $18 billion, and set a first fiscal-2031 range of $70–90 billion. Management framed a roughly $400 billion addressable market by 2030. The July Google custom-silicon agreement is the backdrop, not a new filing today.
items.impact: This is why MRVL led the book, about +5.8%. It is a 2031 range, not a filled order. Do not add on the first green day. AVGO remains the incumbent on Google's TPU, not a cancelled line.

items.title: Broadcom: TPU v8i is in production
items.what: Broadcom said Google's TPU v8i entered production shipments in its fiscal third quarter and is expected to ramp in the fourth. Anthropic has committed $125.2 billion of TPU capacity over five years.
items.impact: Supports the AVGO line, about +4.2% on the day. Marvell's guide is share of the custom wallet, not a reason to cut AVGO.

items.title: Astera up on the tape, not a new filing
items.what: ALAB rose about 7% on 6 Oct with no same-day release. The last print is still Q2 revenue of $392.4 million. The Q3 guide remains $540–560 million. The bid is the AI tape plus the Scorpio ramp into OCP.
items.impact: Real connectivity exposure, and already extended. Hold. A no-news up day is not a new thesis.

items.title: Nvidia at a record; August is still the last print
items.what: NVDA closed 6 Oct at 239.24, a record, with the market cap near $6 trillion. The S&P 500 closed above 7,800. The last earnings figure on this desk is still the 26 Aug quarter: revenue $96.2 billion, Q3 guide $108 billion ±2%. There is no newer Nvidia print.
items.impact: The core bid is intact. Do not reread August as this week's news, and do not add because the index made a high.

items.title: Bitcoin stalled under about $87,500
items.what: Bitcoin was around $85,500 on 6 Oct after failing to hold above roughly $87,000–$87,500. The sleeve on this desk is EBTC, IBIT and MSTR, with BSOL beside it. EBTC's stock quote is still the prior ASX mark.
items.impact: Hedge, not a new core. No add to the call book on a failed break.

risks.title: The 10-year is the multiple
risks.text: The 10-year closed about 5.28% after printing above 5.35%, a 24-year high. AI orders do not cancel that.

risks.title: Memory gave it back
risks.text: MU and SNDK fell on a green tape. The sleeve is extended. Hold. Do not add.

risks.title: The Marvell range is 2031
risks.text: $70–90 billion is a fiscal-2031 range. The first green day is not the size decision.

risks.title: Tesla is still the satellite
risks.text: No fresh Tesla print in this session. The largest line is not a reason to add.

rewards.title: Custom silicon, twice in one session
rewards.text: Marvell's range and Broadcom's TPU ramp. Hold both. Do not rotate one into the other on the headline.

rewards.title: Nvidia and AMD already on the book
rewards.text: Records with the position already held. No chase.

rewards.title: Astera's guide is the fundamental
rewards.text: Q3 $540–560 million is what the 7% day is leaning on. Extended. Hold.

rewards.title: Crypto sleeve stayed a hedge
rewards.text: Bitcoin failed the break and the book did not need it. Leave EBTC, IBIT, MSTR and BSOL as they are.

stance: Hold. Every option line is the 6 Oct bid/ask mid. Do not chase the Investor Day. Do not put ATOM.AX back.
